insight.insight: A circuit's evidentiary value for a regulatory filing can be measured. A deterministic claim map turns each discovered circuit into a structured Annex IV statement. One then measures how often that statement changes across a pre-registered space of defensible analytic choices (flip rate F, modal share π*). Filing presumes a second competent analyst would reach a compatible claim, so evidence is 'filable' only if π* ≥ 1−α. The study finds that circuit discovery on GPT-2/IOI fails this test, and that circuit size is a hidden outcome variable that can invert pooled statistics.
dependent_results: Headline instability (Abstract; 7.2 The claim flips on three quarters of pairs): F = 0.7316 (95% CI 0.7247–0.7380) against the pre-registered 0.20 threshold. π* = 0.4109, so the evidence is not filable at tolerances requiring 0.95, 0.90 or 0.80.
The two most common claims contradict each other (7.2): early layers/distributed at 41.1% versus late layers/sparse at 28.5%.
Filability fails for every addressee and granularity (7.2, Table 5): even the two-class affected-person COARSE claim flips at 0.3950 with π* 0.7291.
No single axis rescues filing (7.3, Table 6): standardising the evaluation metric leaves F = 0.5939 (CI 0.5803–0.6063), removing 0.1377. Seed removes only 0.0009.
The result holds under maximum pressure (7.4): with the size term removed from the claim and size held fixed, F = 0.2706 (CI 0.2550–0.2859), still above 0.20.
Circuits are near-disjoint (7.1): mean Jaccard is 0.1396, median pairwise Jaccard about 4%, and only 1% of pairs exceed Jaccard 0.8.

The random-null comparison reverses within size (7.5, Table 7): pooled, discovered F is 0.7316 against null 0.6774. With size fixed, discovered is 0.2746 against null 0.4230, so circuits are more stable than random but still not filable.
Circuits are functionally uncorrelated (7.6): Cohen's kappa is 0.0146 despite 0.6028 raw agreement. This rebuts the phantom-specialisation objection.
H4 (7.6): the gap between claim instability and functional instability is 0.3344 pooled. It fails the 0.10 threshold at 6 of 10 sizes and is negative at 5, and is carried by the 500–2,000 edge band.
Size bins are not cherry-picked (5 The claim map, Table 1): F ranges 0.70–0.77 across alternative binnings, and is 0.5733 with no size term.

Structure and claim are driven by different axes (7.3): REML attributes 78.8% of circuit-size variance to the ablation×corruption interaction and only 0.7% to the metric, which is nonetheless the largest driver of claim variance.
Instrument failure (6 Method; 10 Discussion): one of seven discovery objectives fails on all 220 of its cells on the library's canonical task.
key_definitions: Specification (4 Formalism): s = (o, a, d, m, τ, P, r, g), i.e. objective, ablation, corruption, metric, threshold, prompt variant, seed and granularity. Every level comes from a published implementation.
Circuit C(s) ⊆ E (4 Formalism): GPT-2 small's factorised graph has |E| = 32,491 edges and 156 components.
Circuit instability (4 Formalism): D = 1 − Jaccard(C_i, C_j); J̄ is the mean Jaccard similarity over unordered pairs.

Claim map φ (5 The claim map): a deterministic, pre-registered code map from a circuit to an Annex IV statement. φ_overseer is keyed on dominant layer band, then size class, then input segment. φ_affected (Article 86) leads with input segment. Three granularities are nested.

Flip rate F (4 Formalism): the unbiased Gini–Simpson probability that two distinct specifications yield different claim classes, F = 1 − Σ n_c(n_c−1)/(N(N−1)). Its ceiling is 1 − 1/k, which is 0.8889 for 9 classes.
Modal share (4 Formalism): π* = max_c n_c/N.
Within-group flip rate F_within(G) (4 Formalism): weights pairs equally across groups; used to standardise axes or hold size fixed.
Filability (4 Formalism; 8 The filability protocol): evidence is filable at tolerance α iff π* ≥ 1 − α. Pre-registered α values are 0.05, 0.10 and 0.20.
Size-matched random null (7.5): random edge subsets of matched size drawn from the full edge set, R = 1,000 null multiverses.
Functional agreement and kappa (7.6): per-example correct/incorrect agreement between circuits, following Bayat Makou et al.; kappa corrects for chance agreement driven by accuracy.
reasoning_steps: Premise (1 Introduction): an audit is meaningful only if two analysts given the same system and tool reach compatible conclusions, so filed interpretability evidence must be stable across defensible analytic choices.

Grid design (4 Formalism; 6 Method): build a pre-registered crossed grid with every level cited. The design yields 18,480 specifications; one broken objective reduces this to 15,840, and the threshold rule discards 52.3%, leaving 7,561.

Measuring claims rather than circuits (5 The claim map): map each circuit through a fixed, deterministic φ so instability is measured at the level of the regulatory statement, not raw edges, and no language-model variance is added.

Uncertainty (6 Method, Statistics): compute F and π* over all pairs and bootstrap over specifications (B = 10,000), not pairs, because pairs sharing a specification are dependent. No p-values are computed, since the grid is designed rather than sampled.
Testing against filability (7.2): compare π* with 1 − α. All tolerances and all addressee/granularity combinations fail.
Ruling out a single fix (7.3): standardise each axis via F_within and show that residual F stays far above 0.20.
Ruling out size artefacts (5 The claim map; 7.4): vary the size binning, then remove size from the claim and hold it fixed. F stays above threshold at 0.2706.

Fair baseline (7.5): the random null is degenerate at 1,000 edges and above, which depresses its pooled F. Within-size comparison reverses the direction, so discovered circuits carry information but remain unfilable.
Ruling out the equivalence-class objection (7.6): kappa near 0 shows the circuits are functionally different mechanisms, not one mechanism described differently.

General lesson (9 Limitations; 3 What this paper is not claiming): circuit size is an outcome selected by the threshold rule, and it inverts three pooled statistics, so every pooled statistic must be reported with its within-size decomposition.

Operational output (8 The filability protocol): the measurement is packaged as a protocol. The filer declares the specification space and φ, then reports π*, F, discard rates and decompositions, without the regulator having to pick the correct analytic choice.
